description_full: Ardagh Metal Packaging S.A., together with its subsidiaries, operates as a metal beverage can company in Europe, North America, and Brazil. It offers a range of beverage cans for use in sparkling water, soft drinks, beer, wine, flavored malt beverages, energy drinks, and teas, as well as flavored alcoholic beverages to beverage producers. The company was founded in 1932 and is based in Luxembourg, Luxembourg. Ardagh Metal Packaging S.A. operates as a subsidiary of Ardagh Group S.A.

financial_summary: Ardagh Metal Packaging S.A. is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $2.8B market cap on $5.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.

Returns on capital run at 3% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 12% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $276M in free cash flow — roughly 5 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 40.82× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 6.1× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss.

Management returns a meaningful 9.4% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 76% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
